title: Reaction Energy Diagram
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AP Chemistry
description: Interactive reaction coordinate diagram. Students identify the reactants, products, transition state, forward and reverse activation energies, and enthalpy change, switch between exothermic and endothermic reactions, adjust the energies with sliders, and test themselves with a click-to-identify quiz.

educational.topic: Activation Energy and Reaction Energy Diagrams
learningObjectives: Identify reactants, products, the transition state, Ea (forward), Ea (reverse), and delta H on a reaction coordinate diagram
Relate the sign of delta H to whether a reaction is exothermic or endothermic
Explain why Ea (reverse) equals Ea (forward) minus delta H
standards: AP Chemistry CED Unit 5, Topic 5.6: Reaction Energy Profile

controls.label: Switch to Endothermic / Switch to Exothermic
controls.description: Toggles the products above or below the reactants

controls.label: Quiz Me / Show Labels
controls.description: Hides the labels and asks the student to click each named feature

controls.label: Ea (forward)
controls.description: Forward activation energy, 60 to 180 kJ/mol in steps of 5

controls.label: Size of delta H
controls.description: Magnitude of the enthalpy change, 20 to 150 kJ/mol in steps of 5; its sign is set by the reaction type

simulation.modelType: Schematic energy profile on a fixed energy scale
assumptions: Single-step reaction with one transition state
For an endothermic reaction delta H is kept at least 10 kJ/mol below Ea(forward)
The curve shape between the levels is schematic; only the three energy levels carry meaning

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Labeled diagram with hover explanations and a click-to-identify quiz
keyQuestions: From which level is each activation energy measured?
How can you tell from the diagram whether a reaction is exothermic or endothermic?
Why is the reverse barrier larger than the forward barrier for an exothermic reaction?
commonMisconceptions: Measuring activation energy from the bottom of the diagram instead of from the reactants
Confusing delta H with activation energy
Believing an exothermic reaction needs no activation energy
assessmentOpportunities: Built-in quiz reports the number of features identified on the first try
